title: These Bees Cook a Hornet Alive at 116 Degrees (and Survive It)

scenes.text: These bees cook a hornet alive. At 116 degrees.
A giant hornet is 20 times bigger than a honeybee. Thirty of them can wipe out a hive of 30,000 bees in three hours.
So Japanese honeybees don't sting it. Five hundred of them pile on and vibrate.
The ball hits 116 degrees Fahrenheit. The hornet dies at 115. The bees survive up to 122.
Seven degrees. That's the gap between the hornet's death and theirs.

description:
Japanese honeybees defend their hive from giant hornets by forming a ball of around 500 workers around the attacker and vibrating until the core reaches about 116 degrees Fahrenheit (46 to 47 Celsius).
The hornet dies at roughly 115 degrees, while the bees can tolerate up to about 122 degrees. A squad of 20 to 30 hornets can otherwise destroy a 30,000-bee colony in three hours.
Would you rather be stung or slow-cooked? Comment below.
first_comment: The hornet's lethal temperature is about 115 degrees Fahrenheit. The bees can survive 122. Seven degrees is the entire margin. Which animal defence do you think is the cleverest?
